issues.where: front fascia, lower centre and both lower corners
issues.what: No bumper skin. The nose is a flat vertical wall with loose diagonal bars and stick fragments floating in front of it and cutting through each other. Nothing is joined and the intakes do not read as openings.
issues.fix: Rebuild the front bumper as one thickened shell with real intake openings. Delete or attach the floating bar pieces with real joins.

issues.where: rear diffuser and lower rear fascia
issues.what: The diffuser fins are paper-thin triangular shards that poke through the rear valance in different directions. The diffuser floor is a crumpled sheet with whorls in the stripes.
issues.fix: Model the fins as solid strakes at a constant thickness, square to a flat diffuser floor, and join them cleanly to the valance.

issues.what: Thin bright slivers zigzag across the hood and fenders. They are open edges and back faces of single-sided panels, not consistent shut lines. Stripes jump across them.
issues.fix: Give the panels thickness, close the open boundaries and cut real shut lines of even width.

issues.what: Large flat slab faces with flat-shaded planes. Stripes stop dead at facet edges and the fender silhouette is polygonal.
issues.fix: Raise the subdivision level or set proper smoothing and normals, and add support loops only at deliberate creases.

issues.what: The rear fascia is a stack of flat boxes with no transitions between them.
issues.fix: Blend the rear fascia surfaces with real fillets.

issues.where: whole body, worst on hood centre and front fenders
issues.what: Stripes look like crumpled foil: wrinkles, kinks and breaks everywhere, with no continuous flow on any panel. The hood is pinched along the centreline.
issues.fix: Retopologise the body as clean quad patches with G2 continuity, or re-fit it to smooth surfaces. Do not use the noisy mesh as-is.

issues.what: The rear is torn into shards with stair-stepped stripes. The tail lamps, exhaust and diffuser do not read as separate objects.
issues.fix: Rebuild the rear fascia as clean panels. Model the lamps, exhaust tips and diffuser fins as separate solid parts with real joins.

issues.what: The honeycomb grille is only floating wire outlines with no depth or thickness. The intake slats are flat painted stripes.
issues.fix: Model the grille as an extruded hex mesh with wall thickness, set back inside a real opening.

issues.where: side intake behind the door, right of centre
issues.what: A light vertical patch with flipped or missing faces breaks the clay shading.
issues.fix: Recalculate the normals, close the hole and give the intake real depth.

issues.where: left rear wheel arch, inner edge
issues.what: A dark slot opens between the arch and the body. Interior or back faces show through a gap.
issues.fix: Close the wheel-arch liner and give the arch lip thickness.

issues.what: Stripes run straight from the hood into the windscreen. There is no separate glass part and no frame break.
issues.fix: Separate the glass as its own object, inset in a frame with a real gap.

issues.what: Large flat-shaded triangle facets. Stripes kink and break at every facet edge, and fender and hood curves show straight polygon segments.
issues.fix: Apply smooth shading with correct normals, raise the subdivision, and keep hard edges only on deliberate creases.

issues.what: The glasshouse is fused into the body like a car cover. There is no separate windscreen or window glass and no frame gap.
issues.fix: Model the glass as separate inset objects in thickened frames.

issues.what: The exhausts are flat diamond plates with no bores or tubes. The rear deck stripes are crumpled around the lamp recesses.
issues.fix: Model the exhaust tips as hollow tubes with wall thickness, and smooth the rear deck surfaces.

issues.what: Stripes break along the mirror seam.
issues.fix: Weld the symmetry seam and unify the normals across it.

issues.what: The splitter is a very thin plate with a hard bright edge and reads as near paper thin.
issues.fix: Give the splitter real thickness, with a rolled edge.

issues.what: The diffuser blades are flat single-sided planes, paper thin and flat-shaded with no stripe response. The outer right blade sticks out past the body width and nearly reaches the ground.
issues.fix: Thicken the blades, round their edges, trim them to the body width and keep proper ground clearance.

issues.what: A bullseye whorl in the stripes shows a pinched pole or vertex dimple in the nose.
issues.fix: Reroute the topology to remove the pole from the visible surface and relax the area to G2.

issues.what: The intakes and lamp outlines are thin lines on the surface. Stripes run straight across them with no opening, depth or gap. In clay the intakes are blind recesses.
issues.fix: Cut real openings with returned walls and set mesh or lamp parts inside as separate objects.

issues.what: The clay override misses the wheels. They render pink and translucent, so their contact with the ground and their flattening cannot be checked.
issues.fix: Apply the clay material to the wheels and tyres and confirm a slight contact patch.

issues.where: rear fascia centreline and lower taillight edge
issues.what: Stripes break along a vertical mirror seam, and the lower taillight trim edge is saw-toothed.
issues.fix: Weld the symmetry seam and smooth the trim boundary.

issues.what: Hood stripes are slightly lumpy, with mild wobble over the centre.
issues.fix: Fair the hood surface.

issues.where: whole body, worst on hood and front fenders
issues.what: Crumpled-foil stripes with kinks and breaks everywhere. The geometry is essentially identical to car-2 (pixel difference below 1 per cent, with tiny changes only on the front lower lip).
issues.fix: Same as car-2: rebuild the body as clean G2 patches.

issues.what: The rear is shredded into shards with stair-stepped stripes. The lamps, exhaust and fins are not separate parts.
issues.fix: Rebuild the rear fascia and model the lamps, exhaust and fins as separate solid parts.

issues.what: The hex grille is only floating outline wires with no thickness.
issues.fix: Model the grille as an extruded hex mesh in a real opening.

issues.what: A light patch with flipped or missing faces.
issues.fix: Fix the normals and close the faces.

issues.what: Interior or back faces show through a gap at the arch.
issues.fix: Close the arch liner and give the lip thickness.
